knowledge:
- key_parameters: files=Character vector of paths to sorted and indexed BAM files ;; sequences=Character vector specifying which chromosomes/sequences to scan ;; windows=DataFrame of window strand information returned by getStrandFromBamFile ;; annotation=A GRanges object containing genomic features to intersect with windows ;; overlapCol=Character string naming the new column indicating feature overlap ;; groupBy=Character vector of column names to group and split plots by ;; normalizeBy=Character vector of column names to normalize frequencies in plotHist ;; heatmap=Logical indicating whether to plot a heatmap instead of a barplot in plotHist ;; threshold=Numeric value (e.g., 0.7) representing the positive/negative proportion threshold used by filterDNA to identify and filter out double-stranded DNA windows ;; destination=Character string specifying the output path for the filtered BAM file ;; getWin=Logical indicating whether filterDNA should return the window information after filtering
- alternatives: ballgown::gffReadGR=Mentioned as a method to read GTF/GFF files into a GRanges object for use as annotation
- when_to_use: Use this package during quality control of strand-specific RNA-seq data to detect, quantify, and filter out potential double-stranded genomic DNA contamination.
- pitfalls: BAM files must be sorted and indexed, with their index files (.bai) located in the same directory. Sequence names in the sliding windows and the annotation GRanges object must be consistent (e.g., matching 'chr10' vs '10') before running intersectWithFeature.

workflows.name: dna_contamination_analysis_and_filtering
workflows.intent: Quantify strand-specificity across sliding windows, intersect with transcript annotations, plot diagnostics, and filter out double-stranded DNA contamination from BAM files.
input: file.bam (sorted BAM file of RNA-seq reads)
file.bam.bai (BAM index file located in the same directory)
workflows.stages:
1. Calculate strand-specific read counts and coverage across sliding windows using getStrandFromBamFile.
2. Intersect sliding windows with genomic annotations using intersectWithFeature.
3. Plot diagnostic histograms of positive strand proportions using plotHist and read count vs. positive proportion using plotWin.
4. Filter out double-stranded DNA contamination from the BAM file using filterDNA.
5. Compare window distributions before and after filtering using plotHist.
workflows.code:
library(strandCheckR)
files <- system.file(
    "extdata", c("s1.sorted.bam","s2.sorted.bam"), package = "strandCheckR"
    )
win <- getStrandFromBamFile(files, sequences = "10")
# shorten the file name
win$File <- basename(as.character(win$File))
win

head(win[order((win$NbPos+win$NbNeg),decreasing=TRUE),])

fileP <- system.file("extdata","paired.bam",package = "strandCheckR")
winP <- getStrandFromBamFile(fileP, sequences = "10")
winP$File <- basename(as.character(winP$File)) #shorten file name
winP

library(TxDb.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg38.knownGene)
annot <- transcripts(TxDb.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg38.knownGene)
#add chr before the sequence names to be consistent with the annot data
win$Seq <- paste0("chr",win$Seq) 
win <- intersectWithFeature(
    windows = win, annotation = annot, overlapCol = "OverlapTranscript"
    )
win

plotHist(
    windows = win, groupBy = c("File","OverlapTranscript"), 
    normalizeBy = "File", scales = "free_y"
    )

plotHist(
    windows = winP, groupBy = "Type", normalizeBy = "Type", scales = "free_y"
    )

plotHist(
    windows = win, groupBy = c("File","OverlapTranscript"), 
    normalizeBy = "File", heatmap = TRUE
    )

plotWin(win, groupBy = "File")

win2 <- filterDNA(
    file = files[2], sequences = "10", destination = "s2.filter.bam", 
    threshold = 0.7, getWin = TRUE
    )

win2$File <- basename(as.character(win2$File))
win2$File <- factor(win2$File,levels = c("s2.sorted.bam","s2.filter.bam"))
library(ggplot2)
plotHist(win2, groupBy = "File", normalizeBy = "File", scales = "free_y") +
    ggtitle("Histogram of positive proportions over all sliding windows before 
            and after filtering reads coming from double strand DNA")
